title: Choose a Model and Tool for a Business Task
subtitle: Choose from the tools your team can use and test them against the work.

sources.label: GitHub Docs · Pilot a feature or model

scenes.title: Identify the outcome
scenes.body: Use a measurable business outcome to select the first task.
scenes.narration: Imagine you own a small order service. The team says it wants AI to speed up coding, so you pull up the last few routine fixes. One was ready on Tuesday and received its first useful review on Thursday. Across the baseline, the wait was eighteen business hours. That gives us a better starting question. Could a small, well-tested change be easier for a teammate to pick up? Mark that waiting step, then choose a task with a result the reviewer can verify, like fixing the minimum order quantity.
scenes.code:
Ready for review → first human code review
Median wait: 18 business hours
Candidate task: a small order-validator fix
scenes.result: Evidence to inspect: diff and boundary tests
scenes.focus: The symptom is a wait after PR readiness
scenes.action: Mark the delay on the ticket

scenes.title: Write the acceptance cases
scenes.body: Define the evidence a reviewer can reproduce.
scenes.narration: Here is the task a developer could hand to a coding assistant. The order validator accepts zero, and the minimum is one. Put four examples in the ticket. One and five pass. Zero and negative one are rejected. Verify the two existing behaviors as well as the new one. Write the zero test first, run it while the old comparison is still in place, and save the failure. After the fix, run all four cases again. A reviewer can now trace the request to test evidence in the pull request.
scenes.code:
Accept quantities: 1, 5
Reject quantities: 0, -1
Keep the existing validator interface
scenes.result: Regression: zero fails before the fix and passes after
scenes.focus: Zero is the boundary the ticket exposes
scenes.action: Put all four cases in the ticket

scenes.title: Select the working surface
scenes.body: Match the task to the approved working environment.
scenes.narration: Open the validator and its tests in Visual Studio Code. The author can ask Copilot for a plan here, then inspect the changes in the same editor. Claude Code and OpenCode run in the approved corporate Google Cloud workspace. Those remain options when a task benefits from tools that are already available there. This exercise needs a two-file change and a standard test command, so use the editor workflow. Record the tool you selected and where its actions run before discussing model choices.
scenes.code:
Local editor: VS Code with Copilot
Corporate GCP: Claude Code or OpenCode
This task: Copilot in the editor
scenes.result: Remote review and checks use approved access
scenes.focus: VS Code fits the two-file task
scenes.action: Pick the tool and record where it runs

scenes.title: Benchmark two approved models
scenes.body: Give each enabled option identical work and a common quality bar.
scenes.narration: Suppose your organization has enabled two models for this editor. Call them A and B. Prepare eight synthetic cases with known expected behavior. Give each model a fresh copy of the same starting point and the same time limit for each case. A reviewer marks a pass only when the tests, scope, and evidence all meet the ticket. For instance, a working change without its zero regression test still misses the evidence requirement. In a second column, log the minutes the author spent steering the assistant or repairing its output.
scenes.code:
Eight synthetic cases per approved option
Same initial code, task text, and time budget
Pass = cases + focused diff + test evidence

scenes.action: Score the same eight cases for both

scenes.title: Make the trade-off explicit
scenes.body: Evaluate the quality gate and the author effort together.
scenes.narration: In this exercise, A passes seven of eight. B passes eight of eight. The median steering time is two minutes for A and three for B. We agreed up front that every case had to pass, including the regression check. B clears the gate for one extra median minute of author effort. Choose B for the pilot and keep that trade-off visible. If you chose based on speed alone, you would pick A, so test yourself now. Which criterion rules out A, and where would the reviewer see the missing evidence?
scenes.code:
Model A: 7/8 pass | 2 min median steering
Model B: 8/8 pass | 3 min median steering
Gate: every benchmark case passes
scenes.result: Choose B for the scoped pilot
scenes.focus: A missed one case and B met the gate
scenes.action: Choose the model that clears the gate

scenes.title: Keep a decision you can revisit
scenes.body: Record the scope, evidence, and decision owner.
scenes.narration: Save a short note with the task, the tool and model choice, the dated benchmark with its sample size, and the pilot owner. In our example, the engineering lead starts with routine validator fixes in Visual Studio Code. Model B is the better option in these eight synthetic cases. If the organization changes the available model, if the pilot starts touching other parts of the order service, or if review quality slips, bring the choice back for review. Now fill in those four fields for a task your team already handles.

Scope: routine validator fixes
